title: Constant-module sheaves forget coefficients preserving colimits
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme in universe $u$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring with underlying type in universe $u+1$. Let $V:\mathrm{Sheaf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda)\to\mathrm{Sheaf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathrm{Ab})$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] send a module-valued sheaf to its underlying abelian-group-valued sheaf. For every category with objects and arrows in universe $u+1$, $V$ maps every colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] to a colimit cocone. No quasi-compactness or finiteness assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), colimit clause; Tag 03CO (lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves). Formal adjunction route: Mathlib ModuleCat.restrictCoextendScalarsAdj and the equivalence of Z-modules with abelian groups.

proof.text: For a commutative ring Λ, restriction of scalars along ℤ → Λ is left adjoint to coextension (Mathlib ModuleCat.restrictCoextendScalarsAdj). The forgetful functor from ℤ-modules to abelian groups is an equivalence (ModuleCat.forget₂AddCommGroupIsEquivalence). Their composite is definitionally the coefficient forgetful functor, so it is a left adjoint. This step is fully proved in Lean, including the coefficient universes.

Sheaf.composeAndSheafify of that coefficient functor is a left adjoint by Mathlib Sheaf.adjunction. Forgetting module coefficients preserves the sheaf condition, and sheafificationNatIso therefore identifies composeAndSheafify with sheafCompose. Transport the left adjoint across this natural isomorphism and apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. This proves preservation of all colimits of size u+1, with their canonical legs.
